e.title: **一个**把「**谁批的、**按哪一版规则批的、**有没有被改过**」**当成产品本身**的 Go 审批引擎**：`Zubimendi/Tribunal`——**⭐ 逐字**「**an approval workflow engine, built in Go**」**，**并**逐字列出**理赔等场景**；**⭐⭐⭐ 而**它**把审计日志做成**一条全局的**哈希链**：**逐字**「**one global, hash-chained, append-only audit log**」**，**并**逐字声明**「**no `UPDATE` or `DELETE` is permitted against it at all, ever**」**；**⭐ 而**流程版本**一旦发布即不可变**（**由数据库触发器强制**）**，**每笔理赔**钉死**在**它当时那一版**上**；**⭐ 窗口内（**创建与推送**同在 **2026-09-07****）**
e.title_en: A Go approval engine that treats who authorised a decision, under which rule version, and whether the record has since been altered as the product itself: a single global hash-chained append-only audit log where no update or delete is ever permitted, workflow versions that become immutable once published under database trigger enforcement, and every claim pinned to the version in force when it was filed.

e.summary: **Tribunal**（仓库 `Zubimendi/Tribunal`）**是一个**用 Go 写的**审批工作流引擎****——**逐字自述为**「**an approval workflow engine, built in Go**」**，**并**逐字说明**它**面向**费用报销、**保险理赔与**采购申请**这类**「**决定要按正确的人、**正确的顺序走**」**的多步流程**。**本次实测**：**许可 **MIT****、**语言 **Go****、**创建与**最后推送**同为 **2026-09-07**（**⭐ 在**解冻窗口之内**）**、**★0**、**仓库约 **91 KB****、**共 **59 个文件／**11 个 Go 测试文件****。**⭐⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**另一种语言的同题材实现，**以及**仓库里那份给 AI 代理的文件**」**。**⭐⭐⭐ 四处最值得看**：**① **它**先说出**审批流程**三种具体的失败方式**（**代人自批、**规则改过之后**没人说得清**当时**生效的是哪一版、**以及**「**审计日志**」**其实只是**状态列上的**一个时间戳**）**；**② **⭐ 它**把**审计日志**做成**一条全局的**哈希链**，**并**逐字声明**对它的 **`UPDATE` 与 **`DELETE`** 一律禁止**；**③ **⭐ 它**把**流程版本**做成**发布即不可变**（**由**数据库触发器**强制**）**，**每笔理赔**钉死**在**提交时那一版**上**；**④ **⭐ 而**仓库里**给 AI 代理的 **`CURSOR_CONTEXT.md`（**20,917 字节**）**写着**「**这一步**故意**不复用**兄弟项目的那套机制**，**别去**修**」**。**⚠️ 本次**未部署、**未运行**。
e.summary_hk: **Tribunal**（倉庫 `Zubimendi/Tribunal`）**是一個**用 Go 寫的**審批工作流引擎****——**逐字自述為**「**an approval workflow engine, built in Go**」**，**並**逐字說明**它**面向**費用報銷、**保險理賠與**採購申請**這類**「**決定要按正確的人、**正確的順序走**」**的多步流程**。**本次實測**：**許可 MIT**、**語言 Go**、**創建與**最後推送**同為 2026-09-07（**在解凍窗口之內**）**、**★0**、**倉庫約 91 KB****、**共 59 個檔案／**11 個 Go 測試檔案****。**⭐⭐ 本條目屬於本輪主題**「**另一種語言的同題材實現，**以及**倉庫裡那份給 AI 代理的檔案**」**。**⭐⭐⭐ 四處最值得看**：**① **先說出**審批流程**三種具體失敗方式**（**代人自批、**規則改過之後**沒人說得清**當時**生效的是哪一版、**以及**「**審計日誌**」**其實只是**狀態列上的一個時間戳**）**；**② **⭐ 把**審計日誌**做成**一條全局的**哈希鏈**，**並逐字聲明**對它的 `UPDATE` 與 `DELETE`** 一律禁止**；**③ **⭐ 把**流程版本**做成**發布即不可變**（**由數據庫觸發器強制**）**；**④ **⭐ 而**給 AI 代理的 `CURSOR_CONTEXT.md`（**20,917 位元組**）**寫著**「**這裡**故意不復用**兄弟專案的那套機制**，**別去修**」**。**⚠️ 本次**未部署、**未運行**。
e.summary_en: This repository **is an approval workflow engine written in Go**, described verbatim as built for expense reports, insurance claims and procurement requests, that is for any multi-step process where a decision has to move through the right people in the right order. **Measured this round**: MIT licensed, created and last pushed on the same day in early September inside the thaw window, no stars yet, a repository of about ninety kilobytes, and fifty-nine files including eleven Go test files. **This entry belongs to the round theme of the same subject implemented in another language, together with the instruction file for AI coding agents that such repositories now ship.** **Four things are worth reading: it names three specific and boring ways approval workflows fail, namely someone approving their own request because nothing stopped them, a rule change leaving no way to say which rule was in force when a decision was made, and an audit log that is merely a timestamp on a status column and therefore not tamper-evident; it answers with a single global hash-chained append-only audit log against which no update or delete is permitted at all; it makes workflow versions immutable once published, enforced by a database trigger, with every claim pinned to the version in force when it was filed; and its instruction file for AI agents, at nearly twenty-one kilobytes, records that a particular mechanism is deliberately not reused from a sibling project and must not be fixed without rereading why.** **Nothing was deployed and nothing was run this round.**
e.body:
**Tribunal**（仓库 `Zubimendi/Tribunal`）**是一个**用 Go 写的**审批工作流引擎****——**逐字自述为**「**an approval workflow engine, built in Go**」**，**并**逐字说明**它**面向**费用报销、**保险理赔与**采购申请**这类**「**任何**决定要按正确的**人、**正确的**顺序走**」**的多步流程**。**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**另一种语言的同题材实现，**以及**仓库里那份给 AI 代理的文件**」**。

**可核实信息（均仓库元数据与仓库内文件实测）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它先把审批流程**三种具体的失败方式**说出来****——**⭐ 逐字为**：**「**someone approves their own request because nothing stopped them**」**、**「**an approval rule changes and nobody can say for certain what rule was in effect when a specific decision was made months ago**」**、**以及**「**the audit log is a `created_at` timestamp on a status column — informative, but not actually tamper-evident, which means it can**」**——**逐字續**「**’t answer are we sure this wasn**」**——**逐字續**「**’t edited after the fact with anything stronger than we assume so.**」**。**⭐ 本词条认为**这一段的写法**值得单独记**：**⭐ 即**它**没有**先讲**架构**，**而**先讲**三件**在理赔与**采购里**天天发生、**又很无聊的**具体事故**——**⭐ 然后**才说**这套系统**怎么回答它们**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 它把审计日志做成一条**全局的**哈希链**，**并**逐字声明**更新与删除**一律禁止****——**⭐ 逐字为**：**「**every event, from every claim, is written into one global, hash-chained, append-only audit log, so has this record been tampered with has a real, computable answer instead of an assumed one**」**；**⭐ 数据库定义里**逐字为**「**a single global, cryptographically hash-chained, unconditionally append-only table — no `UPDATE` or `DELETE` is permitted against it at all, ever**」**。**⭐ 本词条认为**这一处**是**整条**最有价值的设计点**：**⭐ 即**它把**「**这份记录**有没有**被动过**」**从一句**「**我们相信没有**」**变成**一个**可以计算**的问题**——**⭐ 而**代价是**必须**维护一条**链**（**故**其测试里**专门**有**链的构造、**连续性、**被篡改数据上的校验**与**并发写入的序列化**）**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 流程版本**发布即不可变**，**每笔理赔**钉死在**它当时那一版上****——**⭐ 表结构逐字含** `workflow_definitions`、**`workflow_versions`（**逐字**「**immutable once published, trigger-enforced**」**）**、**`claims`（**逐字**「**pinned to one `workflow_version_id`**」**）**、**`claim_attachments`（**逐字**「**MinIO object references, verified-before-use**」**）与**`audit_log`**；**⭐ 而**其集成测试**逐字覆盖**「**published version 2 never affects claim pinned to version 1**」**与**「**database-level trigger rejects raw `UPDATE` on published stages**」**。**⭐ 本词条认为**这一条**对 RIAA 尤其有用**：**⭐ 即**它**正面回答**了**「**规则改过之后**，**几个月前那笔决定**当时**按的是**哪一版」**——**⭐ 答法是**把**版本**钉在**单据上**，**并**让**版本本身**发布后**不可改**。**⭐⭐ ④ 权限与流程判定**全部在服务端完成**，**并**有**一套**十步授权管线****——**⭐ 包结构逐字含** `internal/workflow`（**定义、**带版本的**阶段图、**发布生命周期）**、**`internal/authtoken`（**逐字**「**Stateless HMAC-SHA256 actor token issue/verify**」**）**、**`internal/audit`（**逐字**「**Hash-chained append + chain verification**」**）**、**`internal/storage`（**逐字**「**MinIO presigned upload + existence check**」**）**、**`internal/claims`（**逐字**「**Full 10-step authorization pipeline + attachments**」**）**、**`internal/observability`（**Prometheus）与**`internal/api`（**Chi 路由、**处理器与**鉴权中间件**）**；**⭐ 单元测试**逐字覆盖**规范化确定性、**令牌的**签发／**校验／**篡改／**过期、**图校验与**条件求值器**；**⭐ 集成测试**逐字覆盖**职责分离（**自批被拒**与**显式允许**、**按理赔限定**的不同审批人）**、**角色与**条件门控的**转移（**六种运算符、**字段与**金额分位）**、**附件**预签名／**上传／**确认（**未验证的附件**不满足**「**需要附件**」**）**与**版本钉死**——**⭐ 本词条认为**这一组测试**说明**它把**「**不该发生的事**」**当成**一等测试对象**。**⭐⭐ ⑤ 仓库里**给 AI 代理的 **`CURSOR_CONTEXT.md`（**20,917 字节**）**写明**「**故意不复用**」的**设计决定****——**⭐ 逐字为**：**「**Read this file first, then `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, then `docs/PRD.md`. The implementation is complete.**」**，**并**逐字续**「**Follow `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**」**——**逐字續**「**’s decisions exactly — including the two places it deliberately does *not* reuse machinery from a sibling project (the condition evaluator) and the one place it deliberately *does* (version immutability) for a different reason than that sibling project had. Both are intentional; don**」**——**逐字續**「**’t fix either without re-reading why.**」**；**⭐ 并**逐字点到**三个**兄弟项目**（**FormFlow、**Switchboard 与**AuthNexus**）**，**其中**逐字说明**「**AuthNexus, a later project, is where real auth belongs; don**」**——**逐字續**「**’t scope-creep it into `internal/authtoken`.**」**。**⭐ 本词条认为**这一份文件**值得记**：**⭐ 即**它**把**「**这里**故意**不按惯例做**」**写成**给代理的**明文指示**，**以防**后来者（**人或 AI）**把**刻意的**设计**当成**疏漏**去「**修好**」**。**⭐⭐ ⑥ ⚠️ 三处**须如实标注**：**① **它**自述为**学习路线上的作业**（**README 逐字含**「**Week 6–7, Project 13 of the backend roadmap**」**）**——**⭐ 故**它**不是**任何机构的**生产系统**；**② **它**创建与**推送**同日**、**★0**、**仓库仅 **91 KB****——**⭐ 即**本次**看不到**后续维护**；**③ **其**代理说明文件**逐字声称**「**实现已完成**」**——**⭐ 而**这与**仓库体量**（**59 个文件）**相符**，**但**本次**未运行**任何测试**，**故**不主张**其**真的通过**。**⭐⭐ ⑦ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[claim-ops]]、**[[claims-api]]、**[[digital-claims-management]]、**[[guidewire-claim-intelligence]] 覆盖**理赔运营、**接口与**数字化**、**[[claims-processing-hack]] 覆盖**理赔处理**——**⭐ 而**本条补上的是**「**把**审批链的**可归责性**（**谁批的、**按哪一版、**有没有被改**）**当成**产品本身**的**开源引擎**」这一形态**；**⭐ 本词条**不对以上任何一条做代码级比较****。

**对 RIAA**：**⭐ 本条最值得借的四件事**：**① **先把**失败方式**写清**，**再讲**架构**；**② **审计**要能回答**「**有没有被改过**」**，**而**不是**只记**一个时间戳**；**③ **规则版本**要**钉在单据上**，**且**发布后**不可改**；**④ **给代理的说明里**要标出**「**这里**故意**与惯例不同**」**，**免得**被**好心改错**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次**没有部署、**没有运行**该引擎**（**未启用数据库、**未发起任何审批、**未做任何哈希链校验**）**，**故**不主张**其**任何安全或**可审计**性质**成立**，**也**不主张**其**测试**通过**。**② ⚠️ 本文**对**审计链、**版本不可变与**职责分离**的描述**全部来自**其 **README 与**仓库内**文档、**测试文件命名与**表结构说明**，**未逐行**读实现**。**③ ⚠️ 未核实**其 **HMAC 令牌**的**密钥管理方式**（**⭐ 本词条**不主张**其**适用于**任何**真实授权场景**）**。**④ ⚠️ 未核实**其 **MinIO 附件**校验**在**真实网络条件下**的行为**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核实**其**与**任何**理赔业务规则**的对应关系**（**⭐ 它**是**通用审批引擎**，**不含**保险条款**）**。**⑥ ⚠️ **未核实**其**与**提到的三个**兄弟项目**的关系**（**⭐ 本词条**只记录**其**自述**）**。**⑦ ⚠️ **窗口状况**：**该仓库**创建与**最后推送**同为 **2026-09-07**（**⭐ 在**解冻窗口之内**）**——**⭐ 而**本条**仍以**形态缺口**记之**：**本条的缺口是**「**把**审批链的可归责性**当成产品本身**的**通用引擎**，**并**把**刻意的设计选择**写进**给 AI 代理的说明**」这一形态**。**⑧ ⚠️ 本条目所记为 2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 并如实提示**：**该引擎**是**开源学习项目**，**不是**任何**合规或**授权系统**，**其**用于**真实理赔审批前**必须**做独立的安全与**合规评估**。

**可核實資訊（均倉庫元資料與倉庫內檔案實測）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它先把審批流程**三種具體的失敗方式**說出來****——**⭐ 逐字為**：**someone approves their own request because nothing stopped them**、**an approval rule changes and nobody can say for certain 即**它**沒有先講架構**，**而**先講**三件在理賠與採購裡天天發生、**又很無聊的具體事故**——**然後才說**這套系統怎麼回答**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 審計日誌是一條**全局哈希鏈**，**並逐字聲明**更新與刪除一律禁止****——**⭐ 逐字為**：**every event, from every claim, is written into one global, unconditionally append-only table — no `UPDATE` or `DELETE` is permitted against it at all, ever**」**。**⭐ 這是整條最有價值的設計點**：**⭐ 即**它把「**這份記錄有沒有被動過**」**從一句**「**我們相信沒有**」**變成一個可以計算的問題**——**⭐ 代價是**必須維護一條鏈**（**故其測試**專門有**鏈的構造、**連續性、**被篡改數據上的校驗與**並發寫入的序列化**）**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 流程版本**發布即不可變**，**每筆理賠釘死在當時那一版上****——**⭐ 表結構逐字含** `workflow_definitions`、**`workflow_versions`（**immutable once published, trigger-enforced**）、**`claims`（**pinned to one `workflow_version_id`**）、**`claim_attachments`（**MinIO object references, verified-before-use**）與 `audit_log`**；**⭐ 集成測試逐字覆蓋**「**published version 2 never affects claim pinned to version 1**」與**「**database-level trigger rejects raw `UPDATE` on published stages**」**。**⭐ 這正面回答了**「**規則改過之後，**幾個月前那筆決定當時按的是哪一版**」**——**⭐ 答法是**把版本釘在單據上**，**並讓版本本身發布後不可改**。**⭐⭐ ④ 權限與流程判定**全部在服務端完成**，**並有一套**十步授權管線****——**⭐ 包結構**含 `internal/workflow`、**`internal/authtoken`（**Stateless HMAC-SHA256 actor token This repository **is an approval workflow engine written in Go**, described verbatim as built for expense reports, insurance claims and procurement requests: any multi-step process where a decision has to move through the right people in the right order. **This entry belongs to the round theme of the same subject implemented in another language, together with the instruction file for AI coding agents that such repositories now ship.**

**Verified information, all measured from repository metadata and the files inside the repository**: **first, it names the failure modes before it describes the architecture.** The readme states that approval workflows fail in three specific, boring and extremely common ways: someone approves their own request because nothing stopped them; an approval rule changes and nobody can say for certain which rule was in effect when a decision was made months ago; and the audit log is a creation timestamp on a status column, informative but not actually tamper-evident, which means it cannot answer whether a record was edited after the fact with anything stronger than an assumption. **That framing is worth copying because it starts from the boring incidents that actually happen in claims and procurement rather than from the architecture.** **Second, the audit log is a single global hash chain, and no update or delete is permitted against it at all, ever.** The readme states that every event from every claim is written into one global hash-chained append-only log, so whether a record has been tampered with has a computable answer instead of an assumed one, and the database definition describes an unconditionally append-only table with cryptographic chaining. **That is the single most valuable design point here: it turns an assurance into a computation, at the cost of maintaining a chain, which is why the tests specifically cover chain construction, continuity, verification on tampered data and serialisation of concurrent appends.** **Third, workflow versions become immutable once published, enforced by a database trigger, and each claim is pinned to the version in force when it was filed.** The schema names definition and version tables described as immutable once published, a claims table pinned to a single version identifier, attachments held as object-store references verified before use, and the audit log; and the integration tests specifically cover that a published later version never affects a claim pinned to an earlier one and that a database-level trigger rejects a raw update on published stages. **That answers a question this project cares about directly: after the rules change, which version governed a decision taken months ago. The answer is to pin the version onto the record and make the version itself unchangeable.** **Fourth, authorisation and transition decisions are made entirely server-side, with a ten-step authorisation pipeline.** The package layout includes workflow definitions with versioned stage graphs and a publish lifecycle, a stateless token issuer and verifier, hash-chained audit append with chain verification, object storage with presigned upload and existence checking, a claims package described as a full ten-step authorisation pipeline with attachments, observability counters and gauges, and an API layer with routing, handlers and authentication middleware. **Unit tests cover canonicalisation determinism, token issue, verification, tampering and expiry, graph validation and the condition evaluator; integration tests cover segregation of duties including self-approval rejection and explicit allowance with distinct approvers scoped per claim, role-gated and condition-gated transitions across six operators, attachment presign, upload and confirm with an unverified attachment failing to satisfy a requirement, and version pinning. That test set treats what must never happen as a first-class subject.** **Fifth, the instruction file for AI agents, at nearly twenty-one kilobytes, records which deliberate deviations must not be fixed.** It opens by telling the reader to read it first and then two design documents, states that the implementation is complete, and then instructs the reader to follow the architecture decisions exactly, **including two places where machinery from a sibling project is deliberately not reused and one place where it deliberately is, for a different reason than the sibling project had, with the warning that both are intentional and must not be fixed without rereading why**. It also names three sibling projects and states that real authentication belongs to a later project and must not be pulled into the token package. **Recording a deliberate deviation as an explicit instruction for agents is worth noting, because it stops a later reader, human or artificial, from treating an intentional design as an omission and helpfully repairing it.** **Sixth, three points must be stated plainly**: the readme describes itself as a week six and seven exercise, project thirteen of a backend roadmap, so it is not any organisation production system; the repository was created and pushed on the same day, has no stars and is about ninety kilobytes, so no later maintenance is visible; and the agent file asserts that the implementation is complete, which matches the file count but was not confirmed here because nothing was run. **Seventh, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries cover claims operations, a claims API, digital claims management, claim intelligence and a claims processing exercise, **while this entry supplies an open-source engine that treats the accountability of an approval chain — who authorised it, under which version, and whether it has since been altered — as the product itself. This entry makes no code-level comparison against any of them.**

**For RIAA**: **four practices transfer: write down the failure modes before the architecture; make the audit trail able to answer whether something was altered rather than merely recording a timestamp; pin the rule version onto the record and make the version unchangeable after publication; and mark deliberate deviations from convention in any instruction file meant for agents so that they are not helpfully corrected.**

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, nothing was deployed and nothing was run**, no database was started, no approval was submitted and no chain was verified, **so no claim is made that its security or auditability properties hold or that its tests pass**. **Second, everything said here about the chain, version immutability and segregation of duties comes from the readme, the repository documentation, test file names and schema descriptions rather than from reading the implementation line by line.** **Third, how its token signing keys are managed was not verified, and this entry does not claim it is suitable for any real authorisation setting. Fourth, the behaviour of its attachment verification under real network conditions was not verified. Fifth, its correspondence with any actual claims business rules was not verified**, since it is a general approval engine carrying no insurance terms. **Sixth, its relationship to the three sibling projects it names was not verified**, only its own account being recorded. **Seventh, on the window: the repository was created and last pushed on the same day in early September, inside the thaw window, yet this entry still records it as a gap in form**, namely **a general engine that treats the accountability of an approval chain as the product and writes its deliberate design choices into an instruction file for AI agents. Eighth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11 and states plainly that the engine is an open-source learning project rather than a compliance or authorisation system, and that independent security and compliance assessment is required before any real claims approval use.**
